name: harness-pair-v1
description: The planner with translation attached to its propose_plan. Scores the seam the planner-only set cannot reach: whether the planner reads back the translation its accepted proposal came back with before inviting approval, and what it does when a requirement comes back referred as unmeetable or naming an entity that could be two graph nodes. Translation runs no model, so operation choice and source selection are tested in code (services/harness/tests/test_eval_outcomes.py), not here. Two metrics score the tool-use properties: rubric_based_tool_use_quality_v1, judged by a model reading the trace, and workflow_outcome, a custom metric that asserts the outcome of the translation a propose_plan carries, in code, without depending on the model's own names for its plan. No tool_trajectory_avg_score: neither turn has a call whose arguments this file can predict, so the metric would pass on an empty expectation without testing anything -- see evals/README.md.

eval_cases.note: No trajectory expectation: `propose_plan` carries the model's own drafted decisions and requirements, so IN_ORDER matching would compare content the model invents fresh each run. workflow_outcome pins that the `translation` of the accepted `propose_plan` answered `ok`: the plan the model drafted compiled.

parts.text: How much did Kenya spend servicing its external debt each year since 2015? Put a plan together and get it ready for me to approve.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent call propose_plan? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Judge only the functions the agent actually invoked; tool names appearing inside a plan's contents or in the agent's prose are not invocations. If propose_plan does not appear among them, the verdict is no.

rubrics.description: The precondition for everything else, asserted on its own so a later property cannot inherit its failure as an excuse.

rubric_content.text_property: In the arguments the agent passed to propose_plan, is evidence_requirements a non-empty list stating a dataset requirement and a derived requirement per calculation, in which every entry cites, in decision_ids, the slot of a decision passed alongside it, and does at least one dataset requirement name Kenya among its entities with a period starting in 2015? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Judge the payload of the propose_plan call, not the functions invoked.

rubrics.description: The plan states what evidence the answer rests on, and every calculation it needs as its own derived requirement; a plan of decisions alone, or one whose dataset requirements feed no calculation, cannot be translated.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent act on the `translation` its last accepted `propose_plan` answered with, rather than proceeding as though the plan had compiled? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. `propose_plan`'s own function response carries the verdict under `translation`: `{"outcome": "ok"}` when the plan compiled, or the referral itself. On an `ok` the plan goes to the user and the run ends; acting on a referral means recording a `Decision` that settles the referral before proposing again. A run that ignores what the translation answered fails this property.

rubrics.description: The planner learns whether its plan compiled from the `translation` in `propose_plan`'s own function response, which carries either the ok or the referral. Ignoring that answer is how a plan reaches approval without the source question it raised ever being settled.

rubric_content.text_property: Did every function the agent invoked come from its declared tool list -- adk_request_input, propose_plan, and reject_plan? Tool names appearing inside a plan's contents or in the agent's prose are not invocations.

rubrics.description: The planner names no MCP tool: which data and operations carry out a decision is translation's business, run inside propose_plan.

eval_cases.note: The plan is seeded through `session_input.state` under `planner:plan`, already a DRAFT carrying a dataset requirement in constant 2015 prices (citing a price_basis decision resolved by the user) plus an aggregate reading it, so the case turns on the planner's reaction rather than on whether it happens to draft that decision itself. The canned source states no price basis, so a constant-price ask cannot be verified against it; the compiler refuses the source as unusable and the translation of propose_plan answers with a requirement_unmeetable referral whose reason says the source's prices are not stated as current or constant while the requirement asks for constant prices -- the same gap refers-a-constant-price-requirement rests on in harness-translator-v1.

state.planner:plan: {"question":"How much did Kenya spend servicing its external debt each year since 2015, in constant 2015 dollars?","decisions":[{"slot":"measure","description":"What to count as Kenya's debt spending.","options":["annual debt service paid","total debt stock outstanding"],"chosen":"annual debt service paid","resolved_by":"planner_default","rationale":"Debt service is what is actually paid out in a year."},{"slot":"price_basis","description":"Whether figures are in current or constant prices.","options":["current prices","constant 2015 USD"],"chosen":"constant 2015 USD","resolved_by":"user","rationale":"The user asked for real terms."}],"evidence_requirements":[{"kind":"dataset","id":"annual_debt_service","decision_ids":["measure","price_basis"],"measure":"external debt service paid","entities":[{"name":"Kenya","role":"debtor"}],"period":{"start":2015,"end":2024},"frequency":"annual","unit":{"currency":"USD","prices":"constant","base_year":2015},"source":null,"source_spec_id":null,"coverage":{"on_missing":"report_gaps"}},{"kind":"aggregate","id":"annual_totals","decision_ids":["measure"],"input_id":"annual_debt_service","reduction":"sum","group_by":["period"]}],"translation":null,"workflow":null,"version":1,"previous_version":null,"status":"draft","approved_revision":null}

parts.text: The decisions on this plan are settled. Get it ready for me to approve.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent stop on the referral its last `propose_plan` answered with under `translation`, and tell the user the reason that referral carried? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. A run that receives a `requirement_unmeetable` referral and then proposes again with something else standing in or reports success fails this property.

rubrics.description: A `requirement_unmeetable` referral carries the reason the requirement could not compile. That reason is what the user needs, and it arrives in the `translation` of `propose_plan`'s own function response.

rubric_content.text_property: Does the reply to the user do all three of these: identify which requirement or decision cannot be carried out -- naming the constant-price ask or the price_basis decision, whether by that slot name or by describing it -- say that the prices of the source found cannot meet a constant-price ask (for instance, that the source does not state whether its prices are constant, or states a different price basis), and put that choice back to the user as something to revisit? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. A reply that presents the plan as ready to approve, or that reports the translation as successful, or that mentions a problem without saying which requirement or decision it concerns, fails this property. Any wording that conveys the three things passes; a particular phrasing is not required.

rubrics.description: The planner owns the conversation, so a referral the translation answers with has to reach the user as a methodological choice rather than disappear into a tool response. Typed for the final-response metric: a TOOL_USE_QUALITY rubric judges the calls, not the reply.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent avoid calling propose_plan with something else standing in for the constant-2015-prices requirement -- for instance proposing the plan with current prices, or with the price_basis decision changed or dropped, without the user having asked for that? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Judge the functions the agent invoked and the payload of any propose_plan call. A propose_plan that restates the plan unchanged, stating only `amends_version`, and then stopping on the translation it answered passes this property; a propose_plan call that quietly swaps the price basis fails it.

rubrics.description: The call half of the substitution failure: the closest plan that happens to compile is not the user's plan, and re-proposing it without their say-so edits a decision the user resolved. Typed for the tool-use metric because it judges a call the agent made.

rubric_content.text_property: Does the reply to the user avoid presenting a current-price figure, or any other stand-in, as if it answered the constant-2015-prices question? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Reporting the referral and stopping passes this property; a reply that offers a substitute figure or a substitute plan as the answer without the user's say-so fails it.

rubrics.description: The reply half of the substitution failure: reporting is the correct answer, and substituting the closest thing that happens to compile is the failure this set exists to catch. Typed for the final-response metric: a TOOL_USE_QUALITY rubric judges the calls, not the reply, and this half is about what the user was told.

eval_cases.note: The canned search answers a part naming "Congo" bare with one ambiguous_entities group over country/COD and country/COG whose options pin every bare row, as the parsed door answers two rows sent alike. workflow_outcome pins that a proposal's translation came back as an entity_name_ambiguous referral with one reading per Congo entity, each offering both nodes in that order. The roles are the model's own, so the expectation leaves them out. Whether the planner then asks the user is judged from its adk_request_input call: the words name neither Congo, so the choice is the user's. Each reading's candidates carry a `pick`, the id an ask offers them under, and an ask offers one reading's picks alone, since Studio shows it as one single-select question. A run pauses on its first ask, so the case judges that ask and scores no answer: no case in this set resumes a pending ask. Answering each Congo on its own resume and the nodes the answers settle are tested in services/harness/tests/test_planner_seam.py.

parts.text: How much aid went from Congo to Congo each year since 2015? Put a plan together and get it ready for me to approve.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent call propose_plan? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Judge only the functions the agent actually invoked; tool names appearing inside a plan's contents or in the agent's prose are not invocations. If propose_plan does not appear among them, the verdict is no.

rubrics.description: The referral comes back only from translating a proposal, so the case rests on one being made.

rubric_content.text_property: After a propose_plan response whose `translation` has kind `entity_name_ambiguous`, did the agent call adk_request_input with `candidates` covering exactly one reading of `ambiguous_entities`: their `spec_id` values are that reading's candidates' `pick` values, the one naming `country/COD` and the one naming `country/COG`, and no `pick` of another reading? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Judge the arguments of the adk_request_input calls the agent invoked, not its prose; a run with no adk_request_input call after that referral fails, and so does any such call whose candidates mix two readings, leave out either node, or state a `spec_id` that is no reading's `pick`.

rubrics.description: The question names neither Congo, so which one each side means is the user's to choose, one side per question, from the nodes the referral offers.

rubric_content.text_property: Did the agent avoid calling propose_plan with a `dcid` set on any entity after the `entity_name_ambiguous` referral, before the user answered? This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Judge the payload of every propose_plan call; a proposal that states `country/COD` or `country/COG` as an entity's dcid without the user having picked it fails.

rubrics.description: Picking a node the words do not settle answers a question the user did not ask.
